skills.name: Industrialisation: effects in Europe and the wider world

note.text: Industrialisation expanded production, urban employment and transport connections, but benefits and costs were distributed unequally. Workers could face dangerous conditions, long hours and insecure housing; trade unions and reform campaigns sought change. Industrial growth increased demand for resources and markets, interacting with imperial expansion and unequal colonial economies. Smoke, waste and crowded settlements affected environments and health. Avoid describing either universal prosperity or nothing but decline: identify whose experience, which mechanism and what period are being considered.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to weigh production and connectivity against labour, environmental and colonial inequalities. Builds on: science, transport and industrial capacity. Leads to: economic expansion, vulnerability and the Great Depression.

sections.heading: Follow the evidence and examples
sections.text: A factory’s output could rise while workers organised over conditions. A railway could connect an export-producing area to a port without serving every local need equally. Such examples show why increased total production does not by itself establish equal gains. Environmental damage and reform efforts also belong to the historical explanation.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: Identify actor, action, place and period before explaining a relationship. Use the practice text only for the claim it supports. Distinguish a cause, an event and an outcome; compare authentic sources before treating an interpretation as established. A sequence alone does not prove that every later outcome was inevitable.

cards.idea: Check a claim against the sequence, setting and limits of the evidence.
example: Higher total output proves every person gained equally. Correction: Distribution and working conditions require separate evidence.
Workers had no agency in responding to industrial change. Correction: Organisation and reform were important responses.
Every colonial railway was designed equally around all local needs. Correction: The purpose and distribution of benefits must be examined.
Industrial growth had no possible effects on surroundings or health. Correction: Pollution and living conditions formed part of its costs.
